newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 4.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Tuesday:
* On Monday, the Dow Jones jumped 41.18 points to 6,918.92. PLDT's ADR increased by $ 3/4 to $58 3/4.
* The peso closed 26.322 to a U.S. dollar from 26.331.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index increased by 5.13 points to 3,320.41
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.53125 percent.
*Metro Pacific Corp (MPC), the local flagship unit of First Pacific Co Ltd, said on Monday it is considering raising its equity interest in Smart Communications Inc from the current 35 percent.
*Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson on Monday denied reports the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had required banks to limit their loan exposures to real estate companies.

Singson's statement came after local newspapers said the Philippine government was considering a specific provision in the country's IMF exit programme limiting to a maximum of 30 percent the real estate loan portfolio of banks. The reports said this was contained in a Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies (MEP) submitted by the Philippine government to an IMF team which recently visited the country.

*Philippine refiner Petron Corp has delayed the shutdown of a 85,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) to August from March as work to regenerate a catalyst has been put back, a company source said on Monday.

*ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp on Monday reported a 22.35 percent growth in net income last year, and analysts said they were expected it to maintain its pace this year despite keener competition among television networks.

ABS-CBN Broadcasting, the media subsidiary of holding company Benpres Holdings Corp, said its net income increased to 1.53 billion pesos ($58.17 million) in 1996 from 1.25 billion pesos the previous year. Gross revenues reached 4.464 billion pesos, up 16.34 percent from 3.837 billion pesos.
*A. Soriano Corp, the holding company of the Soriano family, reported on Monday its net income in 1996 reached 463 million pesos, up from the 1995 figure of 307 million pesos.
*The Philippine benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate dipped to an average of 10.564 percent at Monday's regular weekly Treasury-bill auction from 10.625 percent last week, the Bureau of Treasury said.
*Ionics Circuits Inc said on Monday it had signed a manufacturing and assembly contract with the local unit of TDK Corp of Japan to assemble magnetic heads.

*The Philippine Monetary Board has allowed Pan Malayan Management and Investment Corp to raise its stake in Rizal Commercial Banking Corp to 60 percent from 41 percent, Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes said on Monday.
*Holding company Metro Pacific Corp said on Monday its board had declared a six centavo cash dividend to be given to shareholders as of March 26.

*Bayan Telecommunications Holdings Corp (BayanTel) said on Monday it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Nynex Corp of the United States to expand their telecommunication services in the Philippines.
